title: Express.js Examples
description: Each example belongs to one starter lesson. Follow its setup steps before trying it. These examples need the named tools and do not run in this site playground.

examples.title: Reply to a request
examples.description: A route pairs a method and path with a function. Open GET / to receive this text.

examples.title: Send structured data
examples.description: JSON is a text format for named data. GET /book returns a small object.

examples.title: Read part of a path
examples.description: A colon marks a path input. GET /hello/Ravi places Ravi in req.params.name.

examples.title: Read a query value
examples.description: Query values follow ? in a URL. Visit GET /search?q=cat to read q.

examples.title: Read a JSON body
examples.description: POST can send a body. Send POST /books with Content-Type application/json and body {"title":"Moon Trip"}.

examples.title: Check a number
examples.description: A route value needs checks before maths. GET /double/4 returns a doubled whole number.

examples.title: Run a shared step
examples.description: Middleware runs before a later handler when it calls next. GET / shows the value this middleware placed in res.locals.

examples.title: Group related routes
examples.description: A Router groups routes under a shared prefix. GET /api/books uses both the prefix and inner path.

examples.title: Say when an item is missing
examples.description: A status code tells the client what happened. GET /books/99 returns 404 because this practice item is absent.

examples.title: Point to another route
examples.description: A redirect asks the client to visit another URL. GET /start points to /hello; a browser follows it.

examples.title: Handle a route error
examples.description: An error handler has four inputs. GET /broken throws an error, which the last handler turns into a clear reply.

examples.title: Handle an unknown path
examples.description: A final middleware can reply when no earlier route matched. GET /missing reaches this fallback.
